thread:
leah (prod): Quick sync — Large retail customer asked for a slower deprecation window and an explicit pin option for their storefront models. Can we map out constraints?
ryan (eng): We can add a customer-scoped pin flag but it increases catalog state complexity + storage. How long a window are they asking for?
victor (cs): They want 9 months for pin + migration credits and prefer canary freezes during peak season (Nov–Jan). Asking for SLA on performance parity vs existing pinned model.
sam (eng-ml): Benchmarks we ran: new-model (v2) avg latency 120ms, p95 210ms on our test fleet; old-model (v1) avg 100ms p95 180ms. On embed tasks v2 is +2% recall. Looks acceptable but we need gated evals for their LLM prompts.
leah (prod): So asks: (1) per-tenant pin toggle (non-global), (2) 9-mo pin TTL, (3) benchmark parity guarantee and migration credit. Tradeoffs?
ryan (eng): Tradeoffs: a) per-tenant pins block automated rollout/auto-updates -> operational debt; b) longer TTLs reduce our ability to reclaim compute for new models; c) we can enforce a migration plan: automated sunset reminder at 6mo, 90/30/7-day comm cadence.
sam (eng-ml): For parity guarantee — we should require a benchmark suite (customer-supplied + standard probes). If v2 falls below recall delta >1.5% we roll fallback to v1 for that tenant automatically. Need to codify evaluation hooks in onboard spec.
leah (prod): Draft of acceptance criteria we can propose to customer: 1) run canonical prompt set (their 500 prompts) through our eval harness; 2) p95 latency delta <= +40ms; 3) quality delta <= +1.5% on recall/precision metrics OR explicit manual signoff; 4) opt-in migration credits applied on first 3 months.
victor (cs): They’ll push back on the latency delta; asked for +20ms. We can offer lower delta for extra credits. Also asked that pins be editable via console and API.
ryan (eng): Implementation sketch: add tenant_pin boolean + pin_expires_at timestamp in catalog entries. Routing will check pin first; fallback policy remains. Need migration: background job to surface expiring pins and generate canary tasks. Minimal DB schema change (~2 cols on catalog table).
leah (prod): Impact on rollout automation: flagged tenants should be removed from global canaries and from bulk model swaps. Ops: add a "pinned-tenants" filter in console.
ryan (eng): I can spike this in a small PR: schema + routing layer check + admin API. Estimate: 3 sprint-weeks for eng + 1 sprint for QA/rollout gating.
sam (eng-ml): Evals work: create a tenant benchmark bundle: store as JSONL in S3, hook to bench-runner. If v2 fails threshold, create automatic fallback incident and notify cs + prod.
leah (prod): Comms plan: propose to customer a conditional agreement: we accept 9mo pin if they: (a) provide 500 prompt eval set + latency SLA of +30ms OR pay 2 months extra credits. We also request permission to run canary tests in low-traffic windows.
victor (cs): I’ll draft that in the contract language. Also will ask legal for a pin-exception clause for emergency rollbacks.
ryan (eng): Quick note: need to throttle pinned-tenant bulk operations to avoid thundering herd during catalog migrations. Add rate limiter and an opt-in bulk-swap tool that respects pins.
deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/tenant-pin-spike on staging — run id: ci-2026-03-15-0712. Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/ci-2026-03-15-0712
leah (prod): Next steps: (1) ryan spike + RFC by EOD Thu, (2) sam to draft eval hooks and thresholds, (3) victor to get customer to accept conditional terms, (4) leah to prepare comms + runbook. Tagging owners: @ryan, @sam, @victor. :thumbsup:
